title: Theme pack
description: The interchange language between theme ecosystems and this desk (LEO-289). A pack is a family; a variant is one palette in it. Each variant carries the base24 slot set — the terminal-compatible core, verified against tinted-theming/base24/styling.md: base00-base0F identical to base16, base10/base11 darker background runs, base12-base17 the brights (red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta) — plus an optional `ramp` of the intermediate surface steps the shell reads but base24 does not carry (the ramp is what keeps a source palette's full depth; without it the derivation falls back to the nearest slot). A variant declares kind (`light`|`dark`); a dark one may name its light counterpart, and several may share one. Resolution of a counterpart never fails: a desk with a theme it cannot pair beats a desk with no theme.

pack.description: The family's name. Names the things, not the file that happens to implement them.

accents.description: Which slot answers each accent role the shell's modes may lease (Focus.accentRole names one of these; the shell's set is lavender, blue, peach, mauve, green, pink, teal). A pack must name all seven and each must resolve to a slot its variants carry — two roles landing on one slot would render two modes identically, which is the failure the lease exists to prevent.

id.description: A stable identifier, lowercase alphanumeric with dashes.

kind.description: Which half of the day/night cycle this variant belongs to. The cycle picks between the kinds; the counterpart names how a dark one pairs to a light one.

light-counterpart.description: The variant that reads as the same look in daylight. Optional and only meaningful on a dark variant; several dark variants may name the same light one, which is Catppuccin's shape — three darks over one light — rather than a defect.

base24.description: The base24 slot set, complete. Meanings (per tinted-theming/base24): base00-07 the background ramp, dark-to-light on a dark kind; base08-0F the hues (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, plus base0F's 'dark red or brown'); base10/11 the darker background variants (the depth mantles and crusts live on); base12-17 the brights of red, yellow, green, cyan, blue and magenta — where a scheme's extra hues land without colliding with the terminal eight.

ramp.description: The ramp steps base24's surface slots skip but the derivation needs to stay faithful: the subtexts and overlays between surface2 and text. Absent means the derivation inherits from the nearest base24 slot — a degraded palette, never an error.
